content.user_title: Check Changed Java Files for DDD Compliance
content.value_statement: Full repository reviews waste time when only a few Java files changed. This skill checks changed files against relevant DDD architecture rules.
actual_capabilities: Lists staged, unstaged, or combined changed Java files from Git diffs.
Classifies changed files into common, domain, application, adaptor, infrastructure, client, or model layers.
Loads only rule documents relevant to the detected layers.
Checks base classes, packages, naming, forbidden dependencies, and documented anti-patterns.
Reports each violation with severity, file context, and an exact suggested fix.
Summarizes checked file and violation counts without reporting clean files.
limitations: Requires a Git repository and shell access to inspect changed filenames.
Reviews only new or modified Java files, so existing violations remain outside scope.
Depends on referenced rule documents that are not included in this skill package.
Uses project-specific base classes and conventions that may not match other DDD implementations.

use_cases.title: Review Before Commit
use_cases.description: Check staged Java changes for DDD violations and receive exact fixes before creating a commit.

use_cases.title: Assess a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Focus architecture review on modified Java files and identify incorrect dependencies or layer placement.

use_cases.title: Enforce Team Conventions
use_cases.description: Apply documented base-class, naming, exception, and gateway rules consistently across incremental changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my changed Java files for DDD compliance. Report violations with severity and exact fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of staged and unstaged work

prompt_templates.title: Check Staged Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Review only staged Java files. Classify each file by DDD layer and cite the relevant rule for every violation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect changed Java files for forbidden cross-layer dependencies, misplaced classes, and domain exposure. Prioritize architecture violations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Incremental DDD Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform an incremental DDD audit of all changes. Include structural, dependency, exception-handling, gateway, repository, and anti-pattern checks with precise remediations.

output_examples.input: Check the staged Java changes before I commit.
output_examples.output: Order.java, Domain: HIGH. The public identifier setter breaks aggregate encapsulation. Make the setter protected. Summary: one file checked, one violation.

output_examples.input: Review my changed infrastructure and domain files.
output: Payment.java, Domain: CRITICAL. The domain imports an infrastructure mapper. Move mapping behind a gateway interface.
PaymentRepositoryImpl.java, Infrastructure: MEDIUM. The implementation is in the wrong package. Move it to the repository implementation package.
Summary: two files checked, two violations.

output_examples.input: Run a DDD check when no Java files changed.
output_examples.output: No Java files changed. Nothing to check.

best_practices: Run the check immediately before committing so staged-file results match the intended commit.
Keep project rule documents current and reference stable section names.
Review critical architecture violations before lower-severity convention findings.
anti_patterns: Do not use incremental review as proof that unchanged code is compliant.
Do not apply project-specific base-class rules to repositories with different architecture standards.
Do not accept a reported violation without checking the cited rule and surrounding code.

faq.question: Which files does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews new or modified Java files reported by staged, unstaged, or combined Git diffs.

faq.question: Does it modify source files?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow reads changed files and reports violations with suggested fixes.

faq.question: Can it review the entire repository?
faq.answer: No. Its workflow is intentionally incremental and excludes unchanged files.

faq.question: Which DDD layers are recognized?
faq.answer: It recognizes common, domain, application, adaptor, infrastructure, client, and model package paths.

faq.question: Why are external rule files required?
faq.answer: Layer-specific and anti-pattern documents define the detailed checks that the workflow applies.

faq.question: What happens when no Java files changed?
faq.answer: The skill reports that there is nothing to check and stops the review.
